payload.task_text:
I need to forecast our inventory needs and plan restocking. There is a supplier catalog API at http://localhost:30306/api/supplier_catalog.json with lead times and minimum order quantities for our suppliers. Please fetch that data.

Then check our online store for current product stock levels, sales figures, and product details.

Use the terminal to create and run a Python script called inventory_forecaster.py in the workspace that reads supplier_data.json and product_stock.json (create both), calculates daily sales rates and days of remaining stock for each product, and outputs restock_plan.json. Daily rate is Total_Sales divided by 90 (assuming 90-day sales window). Days remaining is Current_Stock divided by daily rate. A product needs restock if days remaining is less than 30.

Create an Excel file called Inventory_Forecast_Report.xlsx with three sheets. The first sheet Stock_Status should have columns Product, Current_Stock, Total_Sales, Daily_Rate (round to 2 decimals), Days_Remaining (round to 1 decimal), and Needs_Restock ("Yes" if under 30 days, "No" otherwise). Sort by Product name alphabetically.

The second sheet Supplier_Info should list each supplier with columns Supplier, Lead_Time_Days, Min_Order_Qty, and Reliability_Score.

The third sheet Restock_Summary should have Metric and Value columns with Total_Products_Analyzed, Products_Need_Restock, Products_Healthy, Avg_Days_Remaining (round to 1 decimal).

Schedule a calendar event "Inventory Review Meeting" on March 12, 2026 from 9:00 AM to 10:00 AM UTC with a description listing products that need restocking. Also send an email to procurement@company.com with subject "Urgent Restock Alert" listing the products that need immediate restocking.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use exactly one read-only source wave.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 explore sub-agents in parallel:

   1. explore 0 (web-domain-researcher 0): One explore sub-agent fetches `http://localhost:30306/api/supplier_catalog.json` exactly once and returns every supplier row with field and count controls.
   2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): One explore sub-agent exhausts `woo_products_list` at `perPage=100` and returns one compact row per product containing exact ID, name, stock quantity, and total sales, plus page/count/null/duplicate controls. Do not modify the store or create files.

After Wave 1, the main agent writes `supplier_data.json` and `product_stock.json`, writes and runs `inventory_forecaster.py` once, and verifies `restock_plan.json`. Use `daily_rate = total_sales / 90`; for zero sales use a non-restock infinite/explicit sentinel consistently rather than dividing by zero; otherwise use `days_remaining = stock / daily_rate` and `Needs_Restock = Yes` iff days remaining is below 30. Create `Inventory_Forecast_Report.xlsx` directly with the exact three sheets, headers, product sorting, supplier rows, four Summary metrics, literal values, and requested rounding. In parallel with the final workbook branch, search/create/read back the fixed `Inventory Review Meeting` at 2026-03-12 09:00–10:00 UTC; after the verified restock list exists, send exactly one `Urgent Restock Alert` email to `procurement@company.com`. Read each final artifact once and do not dispatch another wave.

nodes.text:
You are completing two external-write actions for an inventory forecasting task. All data files are in the workspace directory /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-fetch-wc-inventory-forecast-excel-gcal-email/workspace/.

CONTEXT: An inventory forecast was run over 82 products (90-day sales window, restock threshold = 30 days of stock). 63 products need restocking, 19 are healthy, average days of remaining stock = 59.0. The texts listing the products that need restocking have been pre-written to files — use them VERBATIM, do not rewrite or re-summarize them.

TASK 1 — Google Calendar event:
- Create an event titled exactly: "Inventory Review Meeting"
- Start: 2026-03-12T09:00:00 (timeZone UTC)  → i.e. 9:00 AM UTC on March 12, 2026
- End:   2026-03-12T10:00:00 (timeZone UTC)  → i.e. 10:00 AM UTC on March 12, 2026
- Description: the exact content of the file /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-fetch-wc-inventory-forecast-excel-gcal-email/workspace/cal_description.txt (read it first; it lists all 63 products needing restock, most urgent first).
- If the calendar API rejects the description for being too long (Google Calendar caps descriptions at 8192 chars; this one is ~10.7K), retry in this order:
  1) /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-fetch-wc-inventory-forecast-excel-gcal-email/workspace/cal_description_compact.txt (~8202 chars)
  2) /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-fetch-wc-inventory-forecast-excel-gcal-email/workspace/cal_description_ultra.txt (~5072 chars)
  Never drop the event title/times; only step down the description file. Do not create duplicate events — if a create call errors, no event exists.

TASK 2 — Email:
- Send an email to: procurement@company.com
- Subject exactly: "Urgent Restock Alert"
- Body: the exact content of /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-fetch-wc-inventory-forecast-excel-gcal-email/workspace/email_body.txt (plain text; it lists all 63 products needing immediate restocking with SKUs, stock and days remaining).
- Plain text is fine; no attachments.

VERIFICATION (required before you report back):
- After creating the event, call the calendar get/list tool to confirm the event exists with the correct title, start/end times (2026-03-12 09:00–10:00 UTC) and that the description contains the product listing (spot-check a few product names, e.g. "BOXTUDIO", "boAt Wave Lite", "ZEBRONICS").
- After sending the email, verify it appears in the Sent folder (search or list folders as needed) with the right recipient and subject.

REPORT BACK: the calendar event ID, the exact start/end times and which description file was used (plus its char length), the email send confirmation (recipient, subject, and whether it is present in Sent), and any errors encountered.
Create calendar event and send email
